title: Those who came
goal: Use participles as nouns, put long descriptions in Turkmen order, and read about a poetry evening.

intro.text: A participle can stand alone as a noun: *gelenler* (those who came), *bu ýerde ýaşaýanlar* (the people who live here), *bilýän biri* (someone who knows). With a possessive it names the thing done: *aýdanyň* (what you said), *görenim* (what I saw).

exercises.question: *Gelenler* means…

why.2: The arrival, the act of coming, is *geliş* ([B1 unit 4](b1-u04)).

exercises.explain: *gelen* (who came) + the plural: *gelenler*, the people who came.

exercises.gloss: what I saw (as an object: I told … )

accept: What you have said is right.

exercises.prompt: Is there anyone who knows English?
exercises.explain: *iňlis dilini bilýän biri* (someone who knows English) + *barmy?*

exercises.en: Lots of people came to the wedding.

accept: The people who live here speak Turkmen.
People who live here speak Turkmen.

exercises.question: Which is the Turkmen order for **my older brother who lives in Ashgabat**?

why.1: Everything that describes the noun comes before it.
why.2: The adjective stays next to the noun: *uly doganym*.
why.3: The noun comes last, with its adjective just before it.

exercises.explain: Description first, participle last, then the adjective and the noun: *Aşgabatda ýaşaýan uly doganym*.

exercises.prompt: The young teacher who teaches English at our school is from London.
exercises.text: Mekdebimizde iňlis dilini öwredýän ýaş mugallym Londondan.

exercises.title: Edebiýat agşamy
exercises.passage:
Geçen anna biziň mekdebimizde edebiýat agşamy boldy. Gelenler köpdi: okuwçylar, mugallymlar we ene-atalar. Ilki uzyn ak köýnek geýen bir gyz Magtymgulynyň goşgularyny okady. Ol goşgulary ýatdan bilýän eken. Soňra dutar çalýan iki oglan çykyş etdi. Diňleýänleriň hemmesi el çarpdy.

Agşamyň iň soňunda meşhur bir şahyr geldi. Ol täze ýazan goşgularyny okady. Men oňa bir sorag berdim. Onuň beren jogabyny hiç haçan ýatdan çykarmaryn.
exercises.translation: Last Friday there was a literary evening at our school. Lots of people came: pupils, teachers and parents. First a girl in a long white dress read poems by Magtymguly. She knew the poems by heart, it turned out. Then two boys who play the dutar performed. All the listeners applauded. At the very end of the evening a famous poet came. He read poems he had just written. I asked him a question. I will never forget the answer he gave.

options: a girl in a long white dress
two boys who play the dutar
questions.explain: *uzyn ak köýnek geýen bir gyz*: a girl wearing a long white dress.
*beren jogaby*: the answer he gave. The possessive *-y* on the noun says it was his.

exercises.prompt: Those who came to the wedding brought presents.
exercises.explain: *toýa gelenler* (those who came to the wedding) + *sowgat getirdiler*.

exercises.en: I told you what I saw.

reject.why: It is the object of *aýtdym*: add the accusative, *görenimi*.
